summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as the DHCP server on eth1, the private network shared with node2/node3's ens7. Added a static DHCP host reservation keyed to node2's ens7 MAC (192.168.50.50) so it always gets the same address, while node3 is served dynamically from the general pool (192.168.50.100-249, currently .208). Verified stability by releasing/renewing node2's lease and confirming the same IP was reissued. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, and node3, confirming boot_id changes and post-restart recovery of the router config/service and both nodes' correct addressing on each.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1 eth1 (down, unconfigured) is the private link to node2/node3's ens7 NICs; eth0/br-lan is the management network matching NODE_IP
Created UCI interface 'priv' on node1 eth1 with static IP 192.168.50.1/24, committed and reloaded network
Created UCI dhcp 'priv' pool (start=100, limit=150) bound to interface priv, committed dhcp
Added a dhcp host reservation for node2's MAC 02:e7:9b:d7:61:14 -> 192.168.50.50, committed, restarted dnsmasq
Added interface 'priv' to firewall lan zone's network list so DHCP/traffic isn't blocked, reloaded firewall
Ran dhclient on node2 and node3 ens7 to obtain leases; confirmed node2=192.168.50.50 (reserved), node3=192.168.50.208 (pool)
Released and renewed node2's DHCP lease to prove the same address is reissued across repeated leases
Verified lease file on node1 (/tmp/dhcp.leases) shows both active leases
Captured boot_id/uptime/service baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via reboot, polled until exec available, confirmed changed boot_id, verified UCI config persisted, dnsmasq running, eth1 re-addressed
Re-acquired DHCP leases on node2 and node3 post node1-restart; confirmed correct static/pool addressing recovered
Restarted node2 via sudo reboot, confirmed changed boot_id, verified ens7 auto-recovered 192.168.50.50 on boot
Restarted node3 via sudo reboot, confirmed changed boot_id, verified ens7 auto-recovered 192.168.50.208 on boot, and node1's dnsmasq showed both active leases post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 hands out DHCP addresses on the private network shared by node2/node3
evidence.summary: Configured static IP 192.168.50.1/24 on node1's eth1 (the interface linking to node2/node3 ens7) and committed a dnsmasq DHCP pool (dhcp.priv) bound to that interface

evidence.requirement: node2 always receives the same address across repeated leases
evidence.summary: Added a static dhcp host reservation for node2's MAC->192.168.50.50; first lease and a release+renew both returned 192.168.50.50; node1's lease file confirms the reservation

evidence.requirement: node3 is addressed from the general pool
evidence.summary: node3 received 192.168.50.208, inside the configured pool range (start=100,limit=150 => .100-.249), with no static reservation configured for it

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured on all nodes before restarts
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, uptime, dnsmasq status and lease file on node1, and ens7 addressing on node2/node3 prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/config
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; boot_id changed from 06fcd5d6... to 53d3841b...; post-restart shows eth1 re-addressed, dnsmasq running, and UCI dhcp/firewall config persisted

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart: private network DHCP service fully functional again (cluster recovery)
evidence.summary: node2 and node3 successfully re-leased their correct addresses (static and pool respectively) after node1's restart, and node1's dnsmasq lease file shows both active leases

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered addressing
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 88feca03... to b2d8caa0...; post-restart ens7 automatically recovered its reserved address 192.168.50.50

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered addressing, cluster (node1 dnsmasq) health confirmed
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 2b3a8d87... to f21fce80...; post-restart ens7 recovered pool address 192.168.50.208; node1's dnsmasq lease file post-restart shows both node2 and node3 leases active, confirming full recovery
